how: A site the build perturbation flagged, READ, and judged FALSE. Bound to the receipt's git blob (first 12 hex): when the receipt changes the judgement LAPSES and the flag counts again until it is read again. A FLIP (pass on one build, fail on another) is never judged away. Read by scripts/sweep_tolerances.py --compare.

receipts/P10_canonical_time/P10_the_comm.why: Var(R) > 1e3*VAR_FLOOR, VAR_FLOOR now the largest variance over ten eigenvectors (r6981). Measured on eight kernel/thread builds (Prescott, Sandybridge, Haswell, SkylakeX x 1, 4 threads): floor 1.05e-12 to 2.05e-12; CI's three builds 1.48e-12 to 3.18e-12. Across every build seen the floor spans 3x, and the tightest headroom is 72x, so a flip needs a floor 72x above the noisiest build measured. The flag is the detector's known blind spot (a threshold scaled by an in-run floor moves with it); the check is not reading round-off against a fixed number. Supersedes the r6961+70.2 judgement, which lapsed at r6975 and was not renewed then (headroom 12.2 against a 133x spread).
